# Preview

Compose an interactive preview with replaceable header, title, actions, content, source and footer slots. Each example lives in its own folder; the MDX page imports its TSX entry. The React examples reuse the counter and its styles from `counter/`.

## Installation

<CodeGroup label="Install Preview">
<CodeTab label="MoyaForge CLI">

```sh
npx @moyarich/moyaforge-cli@latest add preview
```

</CodeTab>
<CodeTab label="shadcn">

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add moyarich/moyaforge/preview
```

</CodeTab>
</CodeGroup>

The `preview` registry item includes the Preview slots, CopyButton, and their styles. The installers add the required npm dependencies:
React, `lucide-react`, and Shiki. These preview dependencies belong to the documentation
frame; the component being demonstrated may have its own dependencies.

## Usage

```mdx
import PreviewExample from "./live-preview/PreviewExample.tsx";

<PreviewExample />
```

```tsx
import {
  Preview,
  PreviewHeader,
  PreviewTitle,
  PreviewActions,
  PreviewCodeToggle,
  PreviewCopyButton,
  PreviewContent,
  PreviewSource,
} from "@/components/ui/components/Preview";
import ButtonExample from "./ButtonExample";
import source from "./ButtonExample.tsx?raw";

<Preview source={source}>
  <PreviewHeader>
    <PreviewTitle>Button</PreviewTitle>
    <PreviewActions>
      <PreviewCodeToggle />
      <PreviewCopyButton />
    </PreviewActions>
  </PreviewHeader>
  <PreviewContent>
    <ButtonExample />
  </PreviewContent>
  <PreviewSource code={source} language="tsx" />
</Preview>;
```

Use `PreviewContent asChild` and `PreviewSource asChild` to compose one DOM-forwarding child, such as a custom layout or editor. `asChild` does not compile or run edited source.

The `?raw` import is supported by Vite. Preview itself does not depend on Vite or MDX; other consumers can pass source strings. You can omit, reorder, or replace slots. The basic `<Preview source={source}>…</Preview>` shorthand still works.

### Custom trigger with `asChild`

Use `asChild` on the code toggle to apply its behavior to a custom button without nesting interactive elements.

```tsx
<PreviewCodeToggle asChild>
  <button type="button" className="my-code-trigger">
    Show source
  </button>
</PreviewCodeToggle>
```

The child must be a single native button or a button-like React component that forwards click handlers and ARIA attributes. For non-button elements, provide your own appropriate accessible semantics and handlers instead of using this trigger.

### CodePreview

Use `CodePreview` for a live demo with one or more named source files. It composes
the standard Preview slots and uses CodeGroup for multiple files. Installing
`code-preview` includes these components and their styles automatically.
CodePreview does not require Monaco, MDX, or Vite.
The `?raw` imports in this example are a Vite convenience for reading source files.

<CodeGroup label="Install CodePreview">
<CodeTab label="MoyaForge CLI">

```sh
npx @moyarich/moyaforge-cli@latest add code-preview
```

</CodeTab>
<CodeTab label="shadcn">

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add moyarich/moyaforge/code-preview
```

</CodeTab>
</CodeGroup>

CodePreview lives in `components/CodePreview`. Its npm dependencies are React, Shiki, and
`lucide-react`; the installers include its component dependencies automatically.

```tsx
import { CodePreview } from "@/components/ui/components/CodePreview";
import Example from "./Example";
import source from "./Example.tsx?raw";
import styles from "./Example.css?raw";

<CodePreview
  title="Example"
  files={[
    { label: "Example.tsx", code: source },
    { label: "Example.css", code: styles },
  ]}
>
  <Example />
</CodePreview>;
```

The first file supplies the toolbar’s copy action; each source tab also has its
own copy control. Source files are highlighted with Shiki using their filename
extension; use a file’s optional `language` field to override it. Unknown languages
render as plain text. File labels must be unique. Source text is preserved by default.
The optional `replacements` prop applies string or RegExp replacement tuples to
all files. Repository docs can explicitly use `CODE_REPLACEMENTS` to make source
imports portable; consuming applications can supply their own rules.

### Show example styles with source tabs

Keep component-specific layout and styling in the example folder. Display those
styles alongside the TSX using `PreviewSource asChild` with a `CodeGroup`:

```tsx
import {
  Preview,
  PreviewHeader,
  PreviewTitle,
  PreviewActions,
  PreviewCodeToggle,
  PreviewCopyButton,
  PreviewContent,
  PreviewSource,
} from "@/components/ui/components/Preview";
import { CodeGroup, CodeTab } from "@/components/ui/components/CodeGroup";
import Example from "./Example";
import source from "./Example.tsx?raw";
import styles from "./Example.css?raw";

export function ExamplePreview() {
  return (
    <Preview title="Example" source={source}>
      <PreviewHeader>
        <PreviewTitle>Example</PreviewTitle>
        <PreviewActions>
          <PreviewCodeToggle />
          <PreviewCopyButton />
        </PreviewActions>
      </PreviewHeader>
      <PreviewContent>
        <Example />
      </PreviewContent>
      <PreviewSource asChild>
        <div>
          <CodeGroup label="Example files">
            <CodeTab label="Example.tsx">
              <pre>
                <code>{source}</code>
              </pre>
            </CodeTab>
            <CodeTab label="Example.css">
              <pre>
                <code>{styles}</code>
              </pre>
            </CodeTab>
          </CodeGroup>
        </div>
      </PreviewSource>
    </Preview>
  );
}
```

`Example.tsx` imports `./Example.css` so the live demo and the displayed source
use the same stylesheet. Preview supplies its own border, spacing, toolbar,
buttons, and source-slot layout. Install `code-group` alongside `preview` when
using this optional composition; Preview does not require CodeGroup itself.

## Styling

Use `--mf-preview-background`, `--mf-preview-border`, `--mf-preview-radius`,
`--mf-preview-padding`, and `--mf-preview-margin` in application CSS.
